clue.text: Salacious girl sent back into corrupt place

indicators.note: into means the reversed name goes inside the place

parts.note: a sty, as in pigsty, is a filthy den of corruption

indicators.note: sent back means the girl's name is written in reverse order

parts.note: Mae is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of a young woman packed off back to some den of iniquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the girl's name round and 'into' puts it inside a pigsty, a byword for a filthy, corrupt place.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a racy, sexually charged story or scene is described as both salacious and steamy.

clue.text: Consult with servant, liquid having soaked through

parts.note: to see a doctor or adviser is to consult them
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: Someone consults their manservant after a leak drips through.
explanation.definitionFit: The fluid that has slowly leaked or oozed through porous material is called by this noun.

clue.text: Dexterous character maybe to strive for longer, collaring crooks at the finish

parts.note: to endeavour is to strive

indicators.note: collaring means the word for longer grabs the letter that follows around its middle

parts.note: more can mean longer, as in 'stay a bit more'

indicators.note: at the finish picks the final letter of crooks

explanation.surface: A deft person strives to stay longer, nabbing crooks in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse, created by Colin Dexter, is a 'Dexterous character', and his rarely used first name is the verb meaning to strive. 'collaring' and 'at the finish' build the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin Dexter's detective, an example of a character from that author; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: See 2
Retreat when sheep surround husband

indicators.note: surround tells us the first pair of words go around the single letter for husband

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer retreats as his flock of sheep crowds round him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surround' makes the word for when and the sheep enclose the husband's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat or hermitage where people withdraw for meditation.

clue.text: With vermouth carried in ship, drunk is waiting patiently

indicators.note: carried in means the vermouth goes inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A boozy sailor with a cargo of vermouth waits quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried in' puts the vermouth inside the ship; 'It' for Italian vermouth comes from the British bar order 'gin and It'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to stay put and do nothing, patiently waiting for things to resolve.

clue.text: Sat in posh car, an American lawyer waves to expose foe

indicators.note: sat in means these letters are placed inside the car

parts.note: RR is a Rolls-Royce, a posh car
an gives the letter A
a DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A US prosecutor sits in a luxury car and waves to reveal an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat in' puts the lawyer inside the Rolls-Royce. The definition is descriptive: radio waves bounce off an enemy to reveal it.
explanation.definitionFit: A system using reflected radio waves to detect hostile aircraft or ships, an example of exposing an enemy.

clue.text: Year lost to our champion at court, in plague

indicators.note: lost to means the abbreviation for year drops out of the champion's name

parts.note: Andy Murray, British tennis champion, a champion on court
taken as written

explanation.surface: The year our tennis champion lost at the court, in a plague year.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Murray is a Scottish tennis player and Wimbledon champion; 'lost to' drops Y from his name.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a pestilence, especially an infectious disease of cattle.

clue.text: Film sons, entertained by topless trollop, getting on down

indicators.note: entertained by means the abbreviation for sons is put inside the shortened word
topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: whore is a cruder word for a trollop
down is soft feathers

explanation.surface: A racy film: sons and a topless trollop getting down to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts WHORE to HORE and 'entertained by' sits S inside. The 1932 Marx Brothers comedy is the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a 1932 Marx Brothers comedy picture, which the single word stands for.

clue.text: Sentimental old Labour leader a new employee of mine

parts.note: tender means soft-hearted or sentimental
Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

explanation.surface: A soppy veteran party boss takes a raw job down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot was leader of the UK Labour Party in the early 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The term began in American mining and ranching camps for a raw newcomer unused to hardship, a novice miner.

clue.text: Closed as theatre, sinister and bleak

definitions.meaning: a theatre with no show running is said to have gone or to be in this state
evil, menacing, as in a shadowy deed
gloomy, without hope, as in a grim outlook

explanation.surface: A shut-down playhouse is a grim and menacing place.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a shut playhouse is 'dark' in stage slang, and the word also means menacing and gloomy.

clue.text: Soldiers in bar drink from this

indicators.note: in means the soldiers go inside the bar

parts.note: a cafe is a small bar or coffee bar
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops in a pub are invited to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: what you drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine or water jug on the table is a vessel from which drink is poured and taken.

clue.text: Ace dropping in perhaps for time at weekend

indicators.note: in means ace and dropping go inside the word for perhaps

parts.note: say means perhaps or for instance
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a turd is a lump of excrement, a dropping

explanation.surface: A pilot drops in for a visit at the weekend, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace dropping' looks like a pilot making a call; it is A plus a crude word for a dropping, put 'in' SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The first day of the British weekend is one particular time falling at the end of the week.

clue.text: Priestess at Sestos has male leave the room

indicators.note: leave means the male's letters depart from the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written, both words' letters; the answer also runs through them, a coincidence of the deletion, since 'male leave' removes letters rather than hiding them
a tom is a male cat, so a male

explanation.surface: A priestess at a Greek shrine orders a man out of her chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' removes T, O and M, in that order, from THE ROOM. In Greek myth the priestess of Aphrodite at Sestos was loved by Leander, who swam the Hellespont to reach her.
explanation.definitionFit: Name from myth: she was the priestess at Sestos whom Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to see.

clue.text: Say two GIs with Ninth tussling over female?

definitions.text: Say two GIs with Ninth tussling over female?

indicators.note: tussling means these letters wrestle themselves into a new order

parts.note: GI written twice gives GIGI

explanation.surface: Two American soldiers brawl with a man from the Ninth regiment over a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tussling' rearranges GIGI, NINTH and F. The whole clue is an example, signalled by 'Say' and the question mark, of soldiers on the same side fighting each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarrelling within one's own side or group, as comrades in arms brawling among themselves would be.

clue.text: Unwise to be disrespectful about leader in Russia

indicators.note: about means the disrespectful word goes around the single letter

parts.note: impudent means cheeky and disrespectful

indicators.note: leader in picks the first letter of Russia

explanation.surface: It is foolish to be rude about the man in charge in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R, the 'leader in' Russia, inside IMPUDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rash, lacking prudence or good sense.

clue.text: Score requires English to follow on in game

indicators.note: to follow means the abbreviation for English comes after on

parts.note: a score is twenty

explanation.surface: A cricket score requires England to enforce the follow-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' places E after ON. The game is the card game also called blackjack or pontoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a card game, also called blackjack or pontoon, where players aim for a hand worth that total.

clue.text: One into 13 visits local worker for mystagogue

indicators.note: into means the numeral goes inside the earlier answer

parts.note: refers to the answer at 13 across, the priestess at Sestos
I is the Roman numeral for one
PH is the abbreviation for public house, a local
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: A worker goes down the pub to visit a priestess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' places I inside the 13-across answer; 'local' is the British word for one's neighbourhood pub, abbreviated PH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both name a priest who initiates others into sacred mysteries, especially in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Astride brother, I want to reproduce with relatives

indicators.note: astride means the word for want sits on either side of the brother

parts.note: need means want, as in lacking

explanation.surface: Sitting on top of my brother, I want to breed with my family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Astride' has the word for want straddle the brother, after I; the clue's order is rearranged for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed from closely related stock, mating within the family line.

clue.text: Knocking back northern beer shows style and vigour

indicators.note: knocking back means the words for northern and beer are read backwards

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Downing a northern brew gives one panache and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' looks like drinking; it turns N + ALE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dash or flair, energetic stylishness in how something is done.

clue.text: Song about People's Republic

indicators.note: about means the song goes around the people

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
men means people

explanation.surface: A song about a communist People's Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People's Republic' looks like one phrase but splits: 'about' wraps the song around the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a former Soviet state in the Caucasus that is now an independent republic.

clue.text: Somewhat excessive answer to letter from Greeks spiteful woman receives

indicators.note: receives means the Greek letter goes inside the word for the spiteful woman

parts.note: a bitch is slang for a spiteful woman
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A nasty woman gets a reply from the Greeks that seems a little over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' puts the Greek letter inside the spiteful woman, after the answer's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something rather over the top, going slightly too far.

clue.text: Persecuted boffin abandoning grand Italian location

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter for grand is dropped from the scientist's name

parts.note: Alan Turing, the codebreaking scientist, was prosecuted and persecuted for homosexuality
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A hounded scientist leaves a grand Italian place.
explanation.walkthrough: Boffin is British slang for a scientist; 'abandoning' removes G from TURING.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a city in Piedmont, northern Italy, so a place in that country.

clue.text: See 23
Sympathy expressed in court for swimmer

indicators.note: in means the exclamation goes inside the word for court

parts.note: to woo is to court
ah is an exclamation expressing sympathy

explanation.surface: A sympathetic sigh in court for someone who swims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' is the verb, to pay suit, not a law court; 'in' puts the sigh inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fast game fish of tropical seas, a swimmer.

clue.text: Antigonus' plea for patience?

parts.note: Antigonus in Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale leaves the stage 'pursued by a ...', so his plea for patience would be addressed to that animal

explanation.walkthrough: Antigonus exits in The Winter's Tale pursued by a bear, the most famous stage direction in Shakespeare; asking for patience, he would plead with the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a request that the listener be patient a little longer, punning on the animal that chases Antigonus.

clue.text: Stuck here, or travelling back from the stars

definitions.meaning: unable to leave our planet, as a grounded creature or person
heading home towards our planet from space

explanation.surface: Stranded on this world, or on the way home from space.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: confined to our planet, and heading towards our planet, as a returning spacecraft is.

clue.text: Prospective partner holds forth to give in kindness

indicators.note: holds means the word for forth sits inside the word for the partner

parts.note: a date is someone you go out with who might become a partner
forth means onwards, as in 'from this day forth', so on

explanation.surface: A would-be partner holds forth about giving things kindly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds forth' looks like a talker's phrase but splits: 'holds' is the container signal and 'forth' the piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something freely out of charity or generosity, especially to a good cause.

clue.text: Old alumnus in turn shows concern for alcohol

indicators.note: in turn means the words for old and alumnus are read from the end backwards

parts.note: aged means old
OB is an old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An old former pupil worries about drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' reverses AGED + OB to give the whole; 'concern' is a business, not a worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish wine shop or cellar is a business, a concern, that sells drink.
